name: October Revolution
also: the Bolshevik seizure of Petrograd, 24–26 October 1917 Old Style (6–8 November New Style); the room from which every later room in this index descends, since the idea contained in Vietnam took its state here
theatre: Petrograd: the Smolny Institute, the Peter and Paul Fortress, the bridges over the Neva, the Winter Palace; the cruiser Aurora on the river

sides.who: Lenin, Trotsky (chairman of the Soviet and of its Military Revolutionary Committee), Sverdlov, Dybenko (the Baltic sailors), Kamenev (who voted against and published the plan); Red Guards 20,000–30,000; Baltic Fleet sailors about 10,000; most of the Petrograd garrison, neutral or with them
sides.backed: the Left SRs at the Congress; the Petrograd factories; Germany's money the previous spring, for the train and the press, not for the night

sides.who: Kerensky (Minister-President), Krasnov (the Cossacks he went to fetch); at the palace 500–1,000 cadets and volunteers and the 1st Petrograd Women's Battalion, about 1,000
sides.backed: the Allies on paper; nobody in the city on the night

chain.did: From Finland and then from hiding in Petrograd, wrote to the Central Committee that delay was death; won the vote of 10 October, 10–2; arrived at Smolny in disguise on the night of the 24th and pushed the rising to finish before the Congress opened, so the Congress would ratify a fact.

As chairman of the Soviet, built the Military Revolutionary Committee on 16 October as a defensive body and used it as the instrument: the garrison's regiments answered to it, not to the government, by the 21st. Took the bridges, the telegraph, the stations, the power plant on the 24th–25th; the palace last.

Closed the Bolshevik papers on the morning of the 24th, which was the provocation the MRC needed; left the palace by car on the morning of the 25th to find troops at the front; found Krasnov and about 700 Cossacks; lost at Pulkovo on the 30th; left Russia in 1918.

The order of the 25th to occupy the buildings; the ultimatum to the palace at 6:30 p.m.; the blank shot from the Aurora at 9:40 p.m. as the signal; the arrest of the cabinet in the Malachite Room at 2:10 a.m. on the 26th, by Antonov-Ovseenko.

chain.who: The Second All-Russian Congress of Soviets
chain.did: Opened at Smolny at 10:40 p.m. on the 25th with the palace not yet taken; the Mensheviks and Right SRs walked out into what Trotsky called the dustbin of history; on the 26th passed the Decree on Peace and the Decree on Land and named the Council of People's Commissars, Lenin its chairman.

phases.name: July Days
phases.text: 16–17 July: half a million in the streets demanding Soviet power, without the party's order; the government fires; hundreds dead; Lenin flees to Finland; Trotsky is jailed. The rising the Bolsheviks did not want, and learned from.

phases.name: Kornilov
phases.text: August: the commander-in-chief moves on Petrograd; Kerensky arms the Soviet to stop him; the Bolsheviks come out of jail with rifles the government gave them and a majority in the Soviet by September.

phases.name: The night
phases.text: 24–26 October: the papers closed, the bridges raised and retaken, the buildings occupied, the Aurora, the palace at 2:10 a.m., the Congress. Fewer than a dozen dead in the capital; six on the government side at the palace by most counts.

phases.name: The ratification, and its refusal
phases.text: The Constituent Assembly elected in November: Bolsheviks 175 of 715 seats, SRs 370. It met once, on 5 January 1918, rejected the decrees, and was dissolved the next morning by the sailors on guard. Brest-Litovsk in March; the civil war, 1918–1922, about ten million dead.

gauge.unit: Bolshevik strength in the capital, approximate: party members in Petrograd, by month of 1917

prediction.endingName: The Winter Palace taken, 2:10 a.m. (Old Style)
prediction.unit: hours the Provisional Government still controlled, counted as government buildings still held of the ten the MRC listed, by hour of 25 October Old Style
marks: Bolshevik presses closed; the MRC answers by taking the bridges
Lenin's proclamation: the Provisional Government is deposed — before it was
prediction.note: The line fitted to the buildings lost through the day reaches zero at about eight in the evening; the palace held until ten past two, because a palace with a thousand defenders and a cabinet inside is not a telegraph office, and because the MRC waited for the Aurora and for the cadets to drift away rather than storm it. The six hours of error are the difference between a building and a symbol. Eisenstein filmed the storming in 1927 with more extras than there had been attackers.

cost.v: fewer than a dozen; the Soviet later filmed a battle
about 1,000; the real fighting of the revolution
715 seats; Bolsheviks 175; one day of session
1918–1922, about 10,000,000 dead, most of them civilians, of famine and typhus as much as of arms
a state, an army and a capital: see the idea timeline in project 55, where 1917 is the second line

outcome: A party of perhaps 350,000 in a country of 150 million took the capital in a night with almost no one killed, and held it for seventy-four years. The revolution was the ratification; the seizure was the night before; the war was after. Every room in this index that contains an idea is downstream of this one.
open: Whether it was a coup or a revolution: the night was a coup by any definition, the Congress that ratified it had a Bolshevik–Left SR majority, and the Assembly elected a month later did not. Both facts are in the room.
Whether Kerensky could have held: the garrison had gone over by the 21st; the question is whether September's decisions or July's made that so.
Whether the Assembly's dissolution on 6 January 1918, not the night of 25 October, is the date the idea stopped asking for consent.

text: The October Revolution as a war room to the standard: the night by the hour, the chain that decided and executed it, the almost-no-one it killed, the ten million who died in what it opened, and the line that reaches zero six hours before the palace fell.
